title: synthetic-probe-factory-architecture-and-on-demand-api-manifest-2025
author: Aisha Patel
body:
> **Archived 2025-09-03:** this page is superseded by "synthetic-probe-factory-architecture-and-on-demand-api-manifest-2026" and is kept for reference only.

Summary

The Synthetic Probe Factory is an on-demand service that fabricates, versions and serves synthetic evaluation probes for Redwood's eval harness, shadow fleets and canary pipelines. It offers:

- A deterministic generation API (REST + batch) with reproducible seeds.
- A metadata, lineage and artifact registry for probe provenance.
- Built-in cost accounting and per-tenant quotas.
- Governance hooks for privacy, label review and deprecation.

Goals and non-goals

Goals:
1. Cut manual probe curation time by 70% for common workload families.
2. Make every synthetic probe reproducible and auditable.
3. Offer a low-latency path for small batches (<= 1k) and a scalable batch path for large fabrications.
4. Plug into the eval mesh and shadow orchestrator so probes can reach private/dedicated environments with safe defaults.

Non-goals:
- Replacing human-authored gold datasets; the factory supplements human annotation for high-risk slices.
- Running large-scale human labeling; review tasks are handed to the annotator UI.

Motivation

Targeted probes for emergent instruction patterns, long-context coherence, functioncall edge cases and quantization stress took too long to produce. Teams reused stale assets or wrote one-off generators, leading to duplication and provenance gaps. The factory centralizes generation patterns, enforces reproducibility and adds cost controls to keep eval spend in check.

High-level architecture

Logical services:

- Probe API Frontend: /v1/generate and /v1/batch, authentication, quota checks, request enrichment.
- Generator Workers: stateless pods running generation templates (templating engine + model driver), recording seed -> output for deterministic replay.
- Artifact Registry: probes plus metadata (seed, template id, generator version, model fingerprint, annotations) in an object store with a SQL index.
- Provenance Ledger: append-only generation event log for audit and replay.
- Governance Service: policy engine (PII safe-lists, domain restrictions) applied before promotion.
- Cost & Quota Engine: estimates token cost before generation and bills project accounts.

Flow: Client -> Probe API Frontend -> (Quota Check) -> Generator Worker -> Artifact Registry + Provenance Ledger -> Governance Service -> Promotion to Eval Mesh

Data model

| Field | Description | Example |
|-------|-------------|---------|
| probe_id | Unique artifact identifier | probe_20250814_03ab |
| template_id | Generator template ID | tmpl_instr_clarify_v1 |
| seed | RNG seed for replay | 92734123 |
| model_fingerprint | Model name + commit + tokenizer hash | redwood-open-v1@b81e |
| provenance_event | Generation/promotion event ids | ev_1187 |
| tags | Routing facets | [functioncall, long-context] |

Generator templates

A template defines the prompt skeleton, slot types, sampling distributions, post-filters and a risk flag. Templates are versioned in the templates Git repo.

- Slots: user_intent, context_snippet, num_entities, language
- Sampling: uniform, weighted or noise-injection distributions with seedable RNG
- Post-filters: syntax checks, token-length bounds, optional small-model semantic validators

Template example (YAML):

---
template_id: tmpl_functioncall_edge_v1
description: "Generates user prompts that exercise functioncall resolution and ambiguous arg types"
slots:
  user_intent: {type: choice, values: ["book_flight", "order_food", "schedule_meeting"]}
  payload: {type: generator, model: redwood-synth-v0, max_tokens: 120}
post_filters:
  - max_tokens: 200
  - banned_patterns: ["\u003cscript\u003e", "SSN"]

API surface

1) Generate (small batches)
POST /v1/generate
{
  "template_id": "tmpl_functioncall_edge_v1",
  "count": 50,
  "seed": 12345,
  "target_tenant": "team-payments",
  "privacy_mode": "redact-sensitive"
}
Returns 202 Accepted with batch_id and estimated_token_cost; artifact_ids are listed at /v1/artifacts?batch_id=... once complete.

2) Batch Fabrication (asynchronous)
POST /v1/batch accepts a CSV or manifest with column mappings and returns job_id.

3) Replay
GET /v1/replay?probe_id=probe_20250814_03ab returns seed, template_id, generator_version and model_fingerprint, and can trigger sandboxed re-generation.

Security and privacy

- PII blocking: templates declare sensitive slots; Governance applies deterministic redaction -> small-model validator -> human review for promoted artifacts with non-zero risk score.
- Tenant isolation: private/dedicated runs use 'local-only' mode with generator workers inside the customer VPC.
- Access control: OAuth scopes probe:read, probe:write, probe:promote. Promotion to the eval mesh also needs eval:promote plus governance approval for restricted templates.

Cost model and quotas

- The pre-flight estimator returns token cost and runtime estimates, with tenant-level multipliers (dedicated tenants get discounts).
- Default quotas: small-burst (<= 1k probes) per project/day = 5 jobs; large-batch jobs capped by monthly credit. Quotas soft-fail, with an override workflow for emergencies.

Operational runbook (SRE / eval-ops)

1) Normal flow: request -> artifacts index ticket -> generator workers start -> artifacts land in registry -> governance checks -> promotion to staging-eval.
2) Failure modes:
  - Job stuck in PENDING: check the generator worker autoscaler and queue depth; scale the generator-workers deployment and review worker logs (task timeout typically 60s).
  - High governance rejection rate: run a sample through the local validator with the template debug flag and open a template patch PR.
  - Token cost spikes: find the job in the Cost Engine dashboard, revoke risky templates, notify the owner.

SLOs and observability

- Probe API Frontend availability: 99.95% monthly.
- Median single-request latency (<= 5 probes): 1.2s target.
- Batch job completion P95 for <= 10k probes: 45 minutes.
- Provenance write success rate: 99.99%

Per-event telemetry: template_id, seed, model_fingerprint, token_usage_estimated, token_usage_actual, governance_decision, tenant_id, job_id

Promotion workflow

States: DRAFT (local only) -> STAGING (internal eval mesh shadow runs) -> PROMOTED (canary/cross-tenant synthetic runs).

Checklist:
1. Automated governance policy pass
2. Privacy redaction OK or human review approved
3. Cost estimate within tenant budget
4. Reviewer sign-off when risk_flag == high

Template author onboarding

1. Add the template with metadata and unit tests to the templates repo.
2. Generate locally with a seed and attach the sample to the PR.
3. Supply risk classification and sample counts.
4. Request review from the Template Review board.

Usage examples

- Quant kernel stress: template tmpl_longcontext_compression_stress_v1, count 2k, privacy_mode strict, target_tenant internal-quant, batch with replay enabled.
- Functioncall canary: /v1/generate template_id=tmpl_functioncall_edge_v1 count=200 seed=9876 target_tenant=canary-team, then promote to STAGING and route to the shadow fleet with quant-fallback.

Auditability

- Promoted artifacts with human review record reviewer id(s) in the provenance ledger.
- Ledger exports (CSV + manifest) for compliance audits are delivered as time-limited signed URLs to compliance roles.

Appendix A: Example artifact record

probe_id,template_id,seed,model_fingerprint,created_by,created_at,tags,governance_state,artifact_uri
probe_20250814_03ab,tmpl_functioncall_edge_v1,92734123,redwood-open-v1@b81e,a.patel,2025-08-14T10:21:47Z,"functioncall;ambiguous_args",PROMOTED,s3://artifacts/probe_20250814_03ab.json

Appendix B: Troubleshooting

- Malformed probes: re-run with debug=true, check worker logs and model_fingerprint for drift.
- Replay mismatch: compare seed, template_id and generator_version against the provenance event; roll back the template version if needed.

Appendix C: Roadmap

- Next quarter: VPC-local generator workers for private deployments.
- Following quarter: streaming generation mode for real-time synthetic traffic.
